Action Plan:
1) Schedule and complete an in-person GP/neurology-focused assessment today in Central London to evaluate unilateral left-sided hearing loss with facial numbness and tinnitus; perform a focused neurological examination and ear examination (otoscopy) to confirm Bell's palsy or identify alternative etiologies; admin to book and patient to contact support to secure a slot; ensure the appointment occurs today.
2) Provide reassurance and discuss management plan after the examination based on exam findings; currently no life-threatening process suspected from the tele-visit.
3) Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Subjective:
- Presenting complaint: 40-year-old female with 3 weeks of left-sided hearing loss and numbness of the left face (around the jawline near the ear), plus occasional tinnitus.
- Onset and progression: Symptoms began ~3 weeks ago; persistent to present.
- Laterality: Left side only.
- Associated symptoms: Ringing in the left ear; occasional dizziness when ringing occurs; no weakness elsewhere; no difficulty swallowing or speaking; no vision changes; no fever; no ear discharge or ear pain.
- Relevant history: History of nasal polyps; past labyrinthitis (not ongoing); nasal spray PRN; Rennies PRN; no regular medications.
- Allergies: Latex.
- Medications: Nasal spray (prescription-like, name not recalled); Rennies PRN.
- Social history: Jockey; current training reduced due to symptoms; lives with partner.
- Family history: Brother with Neurofibromatosis.
- Other concerns: Anxiety about seriousness of symptoms; wants clarification and reassurance; prefers in-person assessment today.
- Consent: Verbal consent for transcription obtained.

Objective:
- No objective vital signs or physical examination findings documented in this tele-visit.
- No imaging or labs obtained or reviewed during this encounter.
- Ear discharge, ear pain, fever, and other systemic signs not reported.
- No documented ocular or other cranial nerve findings on exam (not performed).

Assessment & Plan:
1. Bell's palsy (probable) with unilateral left hearing loss and left facial numbness
   - Assessment: Bell's palsy considered as the likely diagnosis pending in-person neurological and ear examination.
   - Investigations planned: In-person neurological examination; ear examination (including internal ear assessment) to support diagnosis and rule out other etiologies.
   - Treatment planned: No medications prescribed at this visit; management to be determined after physical exam.
   - Referrals: In-person GP clinic assessment today in Central London; admin to book; patient to ring support team to secure a convenient slot.
   - Additional notes: If exam confirms Bell's palsy, further management decisions to be made at that time.

Quality checks:
- Missing but clinically expected elements: Current vital signs, full physical examination findings, and any imaging/lab results are not available from this tele-visit.
- Internal conflicts: None identified.
- Transcript quality: Tele-visit content is coherent; no major audio issues detected; sufficient to plan in-person assessment.

(End of note)
